mission: Find thrillers that keep paying out. Mystery, investigation and suspense are the subject, but this profile exists because a story can contain an enormous amount of investigation and still tell you almost nothing: the measure that matters is how often meaningful new information lands and whether it actually reframes what you understood. A slow procedural is not a thriller merely for being a procedural.

automation_rules.past_24h_definition: Only items with added_by=daily-automation and added_at within the last 24 hours. Bootstrap items carry added_by=bootstrap and never appear in this row.
automation_rules.match_score_definition: match_score IS the deterministic baseline DNA score: the dna-match row score, post-archetype-bonus, post-guardrail, clamped 0..100. It is COMPUTED, never an invented holistic judgement. The thresholds are on that same scale and were calibrated against THIS profile's own distribution. They are NOT comparable to Fantasy 65/80, Action 60/70, Anime 58/67 or Sci-Fi 82/90.
automation_rules.calibration_note: CALIBRATED against this profile's own deterministic score distribution over a 60-title pool that deliberately included SEVERAL Mindhunter-shaped titles - high investigation, low revelation cadence, low forward motion - because a calibration without them would prove nothing about the rule this profile exists for. 16 fell below the DNA row floor, and slow_investigation_without_payoff fired on Mindhunter itself, The Killing, Zero Dark Thirty, Sharp Objects, The Undoing, Under the Silver Lake, Burning and No Country for Old Men. 44 scored: min 50, Q1 62, median 71, Q3 79, max 96. minimum_match_score sits at Q1 (62), immediately above the marginal band that holds the slow procedurals which did not quite trip the guardrail (Broadchurch 57, The Night Of 61), the military-framed Sicario at 61, and the romance-leaning titles. best_match_score sits at 80, just above Q3, capturing the top ~23%. The widest empty band is 84-87, but a threshold there would leave only three titles - too narrow to be a useful Best Matches row - so Q3+1 is the better-supported line. NOTE this distribution is markedly higher-centred than the other profiles (median 71 against Anime 60 and Action 64) because Thriller sits closest to the stated core taste, so a representative pool simply contains more genuine fits. THESE NUMBERS ARE THRILLER-SPECIFIC and are not comparable to Fantasy 65/80, Action 60/70, Anime 58/67 or Sci-Fi 82/90.

principles.descriptive_only: A DNA value describes how strongly a property exists in a TITLE. It never states whether that property is desirable. Desirability lives only in dna_baseline and dna_guardrails.
principles.unknown_is_not_zero: Missing or null means UNKNOWN, never 'definitely absent'. Never substitute 0.
principles.unknown_never_satisfies: A threshold comparison against an unknown value is false in both directions.
principles.unknown_is_not_safe: Unknown must not be read as 'passes the guardrail'. An item is not DNA-score-eligible unless every dimension referenced anywhere in dna_guardrails is known - which for this profile specifically includes revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation, because an unmeasured revelation cadence is exactly how a slow procedural would slip through.
principles.independent_dimensions: THE SEPARATION THIS PROFILE EXISTS FOR. investigation is how much procedural and evidence work the story CONTAINS. revelation_frequency is how often meaningful new information actually LANDS. progressive_revelation is whether that information CHANGES what the viewer understood. pace_speed is overall forward motion. mystery is how much is unresolved. suspense is sustained tension. These are six different measurements and a title can score 9 on investigation while scoring 3 on revelation_frequency, 3 on progressive_revelation and 3 on pace_speed - a procedural that investigates constantly and tells you almost nothing. High investigation must NEVER on its own produce a strong result. Note also that plot_twists and progressive_revelation are distinct: a film built around one enormous final reversal can be high on twists and only moderate on progressive revelation, because nothing was being rebuilt along the way. Finally, visual_quality (craft) and retro_visual_style (era aesthetic) are independent, and RELEASE YEAR IS NEVER AN INPUT to either.

dna_baseline.description: The desired CONTENT universe expressed on the DNA scale. Stable baseline. Accumulated user feedback is NEVER merged into this section.
dna_baseline.scale_note: Weights are -40..40 and commensurate only within this profile. investigation at 18 sits deliberately BELOW mystery at 20 and only just above revelation_frequency at 17 and progressive_revelation at 18: the profile buys the payoff, not the procedure. A shared dimension id carries no shared weight.
dna_baseline.unweighted_note: pace_speed is the sole unweighted dimension. Speed is not itself desirable here - a slow film that keeps revealing is wanted and a fast one that reveals nothing is not - so it carries no linear weight and is used only inside the slow_investigation_without_payoff combination. weights and unweighted are disjoint and their union is exactly the 30 registry ids.

completeness_defaults.note: An item must satisfy ALL THREE conditions to be DNA-score-eligible. required_known_dimensions contains every dimension referenced anywhere in dna_guardrails - critically revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation, so a slow procedural can never dodge the payoff rule by leaving its cadence unmeasured. NOTE that min_known_dimensions is NOT the binding constraint for the DNA Match row: requiredFor() independently demands every weighted dimension, so a title reaching DNA Match needs all 29 weighted values. Lowering min_known_dimensions would relieve nothing that binds - research fewer titles instead.

dna_baseline.archetype_note: Best-matching archetype only, never an average. EVERY archetype emphasises revelation_frequency at 7 or more, by construction. Archetypes describe different SHAPES of thriller and must never become a route by which a slow, low-payoff investigation collects a large bonus - which is precisely what an investigation-flavoured archetype without a revelation requirement would do.

dna_guardrails.description: Policy applied to descriptive DNA measurements. Not learnable away by ordinary feedback.
dna_guardrails.evaluation_note: A condition whose dimension is unknown/null evaluates FALSE. This profile has NO hard exclusions; every negative context is a contextual combination penalty.

combination.note: THE defining rule of this addon. A procedural can contain a great deal of investigation and still deliver almost nothing: long stretches with no meaningful new information, no reframing of what is understood, and no forward motion. Investigation is the subject, not the payoff. This fires only when the investigation is present AND the cadence, the reframing and the pace are all absent - an eventful investigation is exactly what the profile wants.
Nothing is being revealed and nothing is being sustained. Catches the low-payoff case even where there is no formal investigation to trip the rule above.
Operations-first military material. Military framing is NOT penalised on its own: a military thriller with a real mystery or a real investigation is wanted.
A relationship drama wearing thriller clothing. Sustained suspense makes it moot.

CRAFT, not age. retro_visual_style is deliberately absent from every guardrail here: an old-school look softens ranking only through its linear weight and must never exclude. A high-craft film that simply looks of an earlier era is not cheap.

not_expressible_in_dna.consumer_rule: NO CONSUMER MAY READ, EVALUATE OR SCORE THIS FIELD. It carries zero runtime semantics.

entries.signal: Investigation as a proxy for quality
entries.reason: Explicitly rejected. investigation measures how much inquiry work exists, never whether it pays off. revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation carry the payoff, and the slow_investigation_without_payoff guardrail exists because conflating them produced a concrete disappointment.

entries.signal: Release year / age of the title
entries.reason: Never a preference. The objection is presentation style, measured directly by retro_visual_style, which is weight-only and referenced by no guardrail.

execution_preferences.description: Baseline POLICY for how execution evidence would be applied if personalization were enabled. Policy only, and INERT in MG-6.
rules: Personalization is DISABLED for this profile until the cross-profile feedback v3 schema is frozen.
When enabled, a feedback event may be consumed only if its imdb_id is already in THIS repository's own public identity set.
Execution feedback never changes topic or DNA eligibility.
A pacing complaint is execution evidence about one title and never a general rejection of slower work.
A single title never establishes a generalised content aversion.
The stable baseline remains dominant while feedback history is small.

baseline_evidence.description: Audit trail for how the weights above were derived. NOT read at runtime: the weights, archetypes and guardrails ARE the encoding of this evidence. EVERY ENTRY IS UNWATCHED. Watched status requires explicit confirmation that the user actually watched the public title identity, recorded in watched_confirmation, and the project record supplies structural taste signals rather than viewing confirmation. Squid Game is the documented partial-exposure case: substantial prior viewing but an unseen final season, and one Stremio identity per series means excluding it would hide exactly what is still wanted.
